# mfx-ds-bot
A Maofuxing integration fork of DS Bot, retaining its Apache-2.0 license and notices. The npm packag
e is **@maofuxing/mfx-ds-bot**; its source remains in `ds-bot/`.
In a Maofuxing client with the conversation navigation integration, install `@maofuxing/mfx-ds-bot@0
.2.4` from **Plugins → Add plugin** using the official npm registry, then fully restart the client.
The **智能体** entry appears in the upper sidebar. Market search requires the selected catalog to have
indexed this package; npm publication alone does not add a search result. Public catalog submission
is currently deferred.
If `ds-bot` is already installed, remove that plugin while keeping its data, restart, then install t
his package. Both use the same Bot data directory and plugin row IDs; do not enable them together. P
reserve any custom data-directory override and change explicit module overrides from `ds-bot` to `@m
aofuxing/mfx-ds-bot`.
This fork publishes the plugin only. The independent desktop app and installation instructions below
belong to the upstream project.
# DS Bot
English | 中文
DS Bot is a bot plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). It turns DSH into bots. You create your own bots,
then talk and work with them.
## Install
**Desktop app (Windows, macOS, Linux)**
The desktop app brings its own DSH, so you don't need to install DSH first. Download it from Release
e desktop app brings its own DSH, so you don't need to install DSH first. Download it from Releases:
- Windows (x64): `DeepSeek-Bot-<version>-win-x64.exe`. Run it; it installs for your user only, witho
ut administrator rights. If Windows shows "Windows protected your PC", select **More info** → **Run

anyway**.
- macOS: `DeepSeek-Bot-<version>-mac-arm64.zip` for an Apple chip, `DeepSeek-Bot-<version>
-mac-x64.zip` for Intel. Safari unzips it by itself; drag **DeepSeek Bot** into **Applications** and
open it. When macOS says it cannot check the app, open **System Settings** → **Privacy & Security**

and select **Open Anyway**.
- Linux (x64): `DeepSeek-Bot-<version>-linux-x86_64.AppImage` runs on e
very distribution — make it executable and open it. It mounts through FUSE 2, which you may need to
install first (`sudo apt install libfuse2t64` on Ubuntu 24.04+, `sudo dnf install fuse-libs` on Fedo
ra, `sudo pacman -S fuse2` on Arch). On Ubuntu 24.04 and later an AppImage can refuse to start (Ubun
tu restricts the sandbox it needs); the `DeepSeek-Bot-<version>-linux-amd64.deb` on Debian/Ubuntu do
es not have this problem and adds a menu entry.
At the first start the app asks where to keep its data and the Bots' files, and offers to copy a Bot
team from your DSH (it only reads your DSH). Set up a model in its settings. The Windows app and th
e Linux AppImage update themselves; the macOS app and the Linux deb tell you when a new version is r
update themselves; the macOS app and the Linux deb tell you when a new version is ready to download.
**As a plugin in DSH**
First install DSH and set up at least one model in it. DS Bot uses the models from DSH.
**DSH Desktop (Windows, macOS)**

1. In the sidebar, select **Plugins** → **Add plugin**.
2. In **Package name or address**, enter `ds

-bot`. In mainland China, set **Registry** to **Mainland China mirror**.
3. Select **Install**, then
**Enable now**. If DSH says the change takes effect at the next start, quit DSH completely and open
now**. If DSH says the change takes effect at the next start, quit DSH completely and open it again.
If npm is not reachable, in step 2 you can also enter the full path of `ds-bot-0.2.1.tgz` downloaded
from Releases, or `github:Fei2411/DS-Bot#v0.2.1&path:/ds-bot` (needs Git).
[该节后续省略]
## Setup
I strongly recommend that you set up your other bots and group chats by just talking to a bot.
### Web search
DS Bot selects its `auto` search provider for the whole profile. If you disable `web-search-auto`, a
lso select another registered search provider in that profile. See Web search and the recovery steps
so select another registered search provider in that profile. See Web search and the recovery steps.
## Features
### Bot
You can do all your talking and work with one bot, in one window. You don't need to worry about the
context behind it. The bot's details page shows its info, and there you can pick the model you want
it to use. You can switch models at any time, but I still recommend that you keep one model for a bo
t for a long time, and switch only when you really need to.
Bots also have memory. A bot remembers what you like and uses it in later work. You can manage its m
emory on the bot's details page, or just tell the bot.
### Main bot
The main bot is your chief. It has very high rights: it manages the other bots and the group chats.
The first time you open DS Bot, there is already a main bot called Chief. Talk to it, and it walks y
ou through the setup.
In short: have a question? Ask the main bot.
### Group chats
DS Bot has group chats. A group chat is a great way to get several bots to work together, but it cle
arly costs more. So DS Bot does this: every group chat has an admin. The admin answers your messages
by default and calls in the other bots for you. You can also @ a bot directly, and it answers you d
irectly: type @ and pick the bot from the list. To give the bots another chat as context, use + → Re
ference a chat in the message box.
Any bot can hand work to another bot with @. That bot does the work on its own, and the group goes o
n. While it works, it keeps the group posted, and the group, the sidebar and its own chat show what
it is doing. When it is done, it posts the result in the group, and the bot that asked for the work
answers. To stop the work, open the group's details.
A group chat has its own memory. What you tell the group stays in the group: its members use it ther
e, and your other chats and the bots outside the group do not see it. You can manage it in the group
other chats and the bots outside the group do not see it. You can manage it in the group's details.
### Capabilities
Settings → **Capabilities** is a shared library of MCP servers, skills and packs. Add a capability t
o a Bot in its settings; it is available from that Bot's next message in its own chat and group chat
s. A local MCP command that a Bot adds needs your approval before it can run. While other Bots use a
capability, only you or a Main Bot can change or delete it.
